inputs: Input | Value
Callset | `WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz` fetched from the object store (315,153,971 bytes, `.tbi` alongside) into a gitignored scratch directory

Reference | UCSC `hg38.analysisSet.fa.gz` (949,157,663 bytes), decompressed with the `chr` prefix stripped from every header → 195 contigs, `samtools faidx`. The VCF's own reference is the NCBI no-alt analysis set **plus hs38d1 decoys**, with contig names spelled UCSC-style minus `chr` (`1_KI270706v1_random`, `M`) — identical to the stripped UCSC names for the 195 shared contigs

entries.title: Are the candidate alleles spelled the way the scorer will read them?

steps.goal: Does every variant in the callset have exactly one spelling, so that an exact-string-matching scorer can be trusted with an indel?

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: For both alleles len(REF) = len(ALT) = 1 and the record carries a single ALT; running bcftools norm -m -both -f <GRCh38 no-chr FASTA> over the BUB1B locus leaves both records byte-identical in CHROM, POS, REF and ALT.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pre-registered before the run; measured in 073. Both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and byte-identical after bcftools norm; the callset's bi-allelic records were already left-aligned, so the scorer's exact-string match cannot miss them on spelling. Decoy records excluded; the seam is not yet a pipeline stage.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Either allele is an indel or sits in a multi-allelic record, or bcftools norm changes its POS, REF or ALT.
hypotheses.statement: Both BUB1B candidate alleles are single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites, so their submission spelling (chromosome, position, REF, ALT) is invariant under bcftools norm (left-alignment and multi-allelic splitting) and an exact-string scorer will match them as the callset spells them.

hands_to.what: step 2's coding-interval join and step 4's suppressed-call mining both join against variant coordinates, and a join against two spellings of the same variant silently loses rows; step 6's submission rows must be spelled exactly as the exact-match scorer requires.

inherits.what: the delivered VCF and the GRCh38 no-chr reference genome, fetched from the object store into scratch and byte-verified — step 1 cannot check a variant's spelling without both files present.

narrative.summary: Normalized the delivered VCF (Variant Call Format — the callset's row-oriented text record format) with `bcftools norm`, which splits multiallelic records (one row naming several alternate alleles) and left-aligns indels (insertions/deletions) against the GRCh38 reference genome. Across 4,968,537 records on the 195 canonical contigs, normalization split 66,639 multiallelic records into 133,278 rows and re-aligned the 39,913 alleles that split produced; zero bi-allelic (single-alternate) records changed spelling anywhere in the callset. The two candidate BUB1B alleles are single-base substitutions at bi-allelic sites, and both records were byte-identical in chromosome, position, reference and alternate allele before and after the run.
narrative.verdict: H008 — supported, committed at confidence 0.83: both BUB1B candidate alleles are canonical single-nucleotide substitutions, unchanged by normalization. The callset as a whole needed normalizing only at its 66,639 multiallelic sites; every bi-allelic record was already spelled the way `bcftools norm` would spell it.
narrative.why: The oracle's scorer matches a submitted variant against the answer key by exact string equality on (chromosome, position, reference, alternate). An indel has more than one valid spelling, and a multiallelic record cannot be submitted as one row at all — so a biologically correct answer typed the wrong way would score zero. This is the first question asked about the data itself, and it has to be settled before any downstream join or submission can be trusted.

steps.goal: Which variants are rare enough and damaging enough to cause an ultra-rare recessive disease, and in which gene?

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Re-running the panel filter (methodology 031, table results.panel_candidates) returns exactly two rows flagged rare and protein-altering, both gene BUB1B, both het, both PASS; the ClinVar site-first join (051) finds the stop_gained and nothing else.
hypotheses.reasoning: Retrospective claim: the test (031, 051) ran before the register existed, so this is a recorded observation, not a pre-registered prediction. Two independent routes (call-first VEP filter, site-first ClinVar join) agree on the same two BUB1B alleles and nothing else in the panel. Phase remains unresolved, which the neutral row records; the claim is about the candidate set, not about trans.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A third rare protein-altering PASS allele in any panel gene, a second panel gene with two such alleles, or either BUB1B allele turning out common in gnomAD or homozygous.
hypotheses.statement: retrospective: filtering the annotated eight-gene MVA panel to alleles that are both rare (gnomAD AF absent or below the recessive cutoff) and protein-altering (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) leaves exactly one candidate biallelic set, and it is in BUB1B: one stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic) and one missense allele (absent from gnomAD), both heterozygous, both PASS.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: In results.gene_biallelic (every coding allele genome-wide annotated by VEP REST), BUB1B is flagged biallelic_pass with n_plp_pass >= 1 and phenotype_rank <= 30, and no other gene satisfies all three conditions at once. Other genes with biallelic_pass true will exist (recessive carriers of two rare missense alleles are common in any genome) but none will combine a pathogenic ClinVar allele with a phenotype rank in the top 30.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pre-registered in 069 before annotation ran; measured in 070. All three conditions hold for BUB1B and for no other gene among 65 biallelic genes genome-wide. Confidence is capped by the coding-only scope (neutral row): the verdict is that no coding gene outranks BUB1B, not that no gene does.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Another gene with biallelic_pass true, at least one ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele, and a phenotype rank of 30 or better; or BUB1B failing to appear as biallelic_pass in the genome-wide table (which would mean the coding-region join or the annotation lost one of its alleles).
hypotheses.statement: No protein-coding gene outside the eight-gene panel carries a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles that outranks the BUB1B pair: BUB1B is the only gene that is biallelic on PASS calls AND carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele AND sits in the top 30 of the panel-blind phenotype ranking.

figures.means: Each number is one more filter applied to the same starting set, computed from `results.gene_biallelic` / `coding_candidates` in methodology entry 070. It is the numeric evidence for H004: every filter narrows the field, and the last two — a pathogenic ClinVar call plus a top phenotype rank — leave exactly one gene, BUB1B.

figures.means: Shows how a five-million-row callset collapses to one gene through independent geometric, annotation and phenotype filters. The log scale is necessary because linear spacing would make every bar after the first invisible; the chart is evidence that no single filter — only their combination — isolates BUB1B.

figures.reads: A horizontal bar chart of the same nine funnel stages, one bar per stage, on a logarithmic survivor-count axis. Bars run from the full callset at the bottom (widest) to the final answer at the top (narrowest), coloured purple (raw input) through blue (machinery) to green (the answer).

hands_to.what: step 3 joins this step's genome-wide gene_biallelic table to the phenotype ranking as its own cross-check (H005); step 4 mines the same table's non-PASS rows for a hiding second allele; step 6's submission design and oracle probe rest on the verdict this step reached.

inherits.what: the raw callset and the public Ensembl gene models from step 0's object store; step 1's guarantee that every variant has one canonical spelling, so the coordinate join this step runs does not silently lose or duplicate a row.

narrative.summary: Built the genome-wide annotation layer the delivered callset lacks: a coding-interval reference from the Ensembl gene models (223,048 intervals across 19,750 genes), a binned range join pulling 38,437 (gene, allele) rows out of the 5,012,204-record callset, and a checkpointed Ensembl VEP (Variant Effect Predictor — the tool that says what a DNA change does to a protein) run to completion over all 38,087 distinct alleles. Filtering to rare (gnomAD population frequency under 1%) and protein-altering (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) alleles on PASS calls, then to genes carrying two such alleles, then to a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic call, then to a top-30 rank in the panel-blind phenotype score, funnels the 5,012,204 starting records down to exactly one gene: BUB1B.
narrative.verdict: H004 supported, committed at 0.93: of 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls, BUB1B is the only one that also carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele and ranks in the phenotype top 30 (it ranks 6th). H003 (retrospective — the panel-only test that ran before this register existed) supported at 0.93: two independent routes agree on the same two alleles, though which parent each allele came from is not yet resolved.
narrative.why: The eight-gene panel used until now was chosen by hand from known Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy biology — a circular prior, since the search finds MVA genes only because it looked at MVA genes. A genome-wide scan is the only way to ask whether some other gene, unbiased by that choice, produces a stronger candidate. Skipping it would leave the BUB1B pair corroborated only by the assumption that produced it.

steps.goal: Does an unbiased genome-wide ranking driven by the child's HPO terms agree with the panel-first candidate list?

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: When the causal gene is confirmed by the oracle, its rank in the proband-only ranking over 5,267 curated genes is 30 or better. BUB1B, the current leading candidate, currently ranks 6.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The oracle confirms a pair in a gene the phenotype ranking places outside the top 200, or in a gene HPO does not curate at all. Either would show the phenotype signal did not carry the answer and that the panel prior was doing the work.
hypotheses.statement: The gene carrying the causal compound-heterozygous pair ranks in the top 30 of a phenotype-driven ranking that never reads the callset, the candidate panel, or any variant.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Once the causal gene is known, its rank is strictly better in the proband-only ranking than in the with-parental ranking. Measured so far on the candidate panel: every one of the seven curated panel genes rises without the term, BUB1B by 8 places.
hypotheses.reasoning: Measured in 067 section 5 before the claim was filed the same day, so it is retrospective in spirit: removing the parental miscarriage term raises every established MVA gene and removes four recurrent-miscarriage genes from the top 20. Applied downstream: gene_biallelic reads the proband-only term set.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The causal gene ranks worse, or unchanged, when the parental term is removed - which would mean the parents' reproductive history carried signal about the child's gene that the child's own features did not.
hypotheses.statement: The parental term HP:0200067 (recurrent spontaneous abortion) degrades the phenotype ranking of the causal gene and should be excluded from the proband's term set.

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Ordering results.gene_biallelic rows with biallelic_pass true by phenotype_rank ascending puts BUB1B first; the second-ranked biallelic gene has a phenotype rank worse than BUB1B's.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pre-registered before the join ran; measured in 071. BUB1B is first by a wide margin (rank 6 vs 150 for the next curated biallelic gene). The neutral row states the residual coupling between the panel literature and HPO curation.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A different biallelic_pass gene with a better (smaller) phenotype rank than BUB1B.
hypotheses.statement: Among all genes that carry a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles genome-wide, BUB1B is the best-ranked gene in the panel-blind phenotype ranking — the two independent signals (DNA-derived biallelic set, symptom-derived gene rank) converge on one gene.

figures.means: Shows two independent instruments — the DNA-derived candidate list on the y-axis, the symptom-derived rank on the x-axis — agreeing on one gene: BUB1B sits alone, far left of every other candidate and left of the rank-30 marker, while the next curated biallelic gene (HSPG2) sits at rank 150.
figures.name: track1-gene-scatter.png
figures.reads: One point per gene with a candidate biallelic set (65 genes). X-axis: phenotype rank on the child's own HPO terms, logarithmic, with uncurated genes parked past a labelled boundary at the far right. Y-axis: count of rare protein-altering alleles in the gene. Filled markers are biallelic on PASS calls; hollow markers are biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued. BUB1B is drawn larger and green; genes with a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele are yellow; other PASS-biallelic genes are blue; rescue-only genes are grey. A dotted vertical line marks phenotype rank 30.

hands_to.what: H005 and H001 are both settled together by the oracle's reply — a confirmed BUB1B pair makes both predictions observed — and that reply is what step 6 spends its first submission on.

inherits.what: step 2's genome-wide gene_biallelic table is what the ranking is joined against for the confirmatory test (H005); the ranking itself needs only public HPO files and ran before step 2 finished, but the cross-check that could have refuted it needed step 2's output to exist.

narrative.summary: Reimplemented Exomiser's hiPHIVE human-only phenotype-matching algorithm in pure Python — no Java virtual machine, under 100 MB of reference data — to rank all 5,267 HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology, a standard vocabulary and graph of clinical features)-annotated genes by how well their curated symptom list matches the child's own HPO terms, without ever reading the panel, the callset or a variant. On the child's own 7 terms (excluding a parental-only term), BUB1B ranks 6th of 5,267, and independently 26th of 18,882 in the unrelated tool Phen2Gene. Joining this ranking to step 2's genome-wide biallelic gene table confirms BUB1B is the best-ranked of the 65 genes carrying a candidate biallelic (two rare protein-altering alleles) set — the next-best is HSPG2, at rank 150.
narrative.verdict: H005 supported, committed at 0.80: BUB1B is first by phenotype rank among genome-wide biallelic candidates, far ahead of the runner-up. H002 supported at 0.86: the parental term HP:0200067 (recurrent spontaneous abortion) does not belong in the child's own term set — every panel gene, BUB1B included, ranks better without it. H001 stays proposed, its prediction conditioned on the oracle.
narrative.why: Every candidate found so far came through an eight-gene panel picked by hand from known Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy biology, which is a circular prior. A phenotype ranking driven only by the child's symptoms is the one check that cannot inherit that bias, because it never sees the panel or the DNA. Without it, agreement between the panel and the DNA proves nothing — it would just be the same assumption checked against itself.

entries.title: Is a second allele hiding in a call the filters discarded, genome-wide?
violations: docs/iteration1/step-4/methodology/072-genome-wide-suppressed-calls.md: names results.gene_biallelic — iteration 1's biallelic candidate table names the pair

steps.goal: Is one of the two alleles hiding in a call the quality filters discarded, rather than absent from the sample?

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: Re-running methodology 049 over results.panel_suppressed returns 20 non-PASS records, all annotated, 0 flagged rare and protein-altering.
hypotheses.reasoning: Retrospective claim on entry 049; recorded observation, not a prediction. Zero of 20 panel non-PASS calls are rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's callability deficit is noted as the limit of what a non-PASS scan can see.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any panel non-PASS allele that is rare and protein-altering.
hypotheses.statement: retrospective: none of the non-PASS calls inside the eight-gene panel is a credible hidden second allele — after VEP annotation, zero are both rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's cluster of filtered calls is a paralogous-read pileup (low allele fraction, all gnomAD-common).

hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.prediction: In results.gene_biallelic, BUB1B has n_nonpass = 0; every gene with biallelic_with_rescue true and biallelic_pass false either lacks a ClinVar pathogenic/LoF allele or has a phenotype rank worse than 30 (or no curation at all).
hypotheses.reasoning: Pre-registered before the genome-wide non-PASS pass ran; measured in 072. BUB1B has no suppressed coding candidate and no rescue-only gene meets the pathogenic/LoF or top-30 condition. Alleles the caller never emitted remain outside this test.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele in BUB1B, or a rescue-only biallelic gene with a pathogenic/LoF allele and a phenotype rank of 30 or better.
hypotheses.statement: Genome-wide, no gene reaches a biallelic set only by rescuing a suppressed (non-PASS) coding call while also carrying a ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele and a top-30 phenotype rank; in particular BUB1B carries no rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, so the BUB1B pair does not depend on a filter rescue and no rescued call adds a third BUB1B candidate.

hands_to.what: step 5's read-level recovery of a partner allele was funded only conditionally, on step 6's oracle reply reporting one allele right and one wrong at rank 1 — a condition step 6's actual full-match reply closed, which is why step 5 never had to run.

inherits.what: step 2's coding_alleles, coding_candidates and gene_biallelic tables keep every FILTER value rather than dropping non-PASS rows — the only reason this question could be asked genome-wide at no extra computational cost.

narrative.summary: Extended a panel-only suppressed-call check (step-0 entry 049, which found 0 of 20 non-PASS panel calls rare and protein-altering) to the whole genome, using the FILTER-tagged coding layer step 2 built. Of the 875 rare, protein-altering coding alleles found genome-wide, 129 sit in calls the variant caller marked non-PASS (dominated by low-mapping-quality and low-quality-by-depth filter reasons). Twenty-six genes only reach a candidate biallelic set if one of those filtered calls is rescued, and none of those 26 also carries a ClinVar pathogenic/loss-of-function allele or a top-30 phenotype rank. BUB1B itself carries zero non-PASS coding alleles.
narrative.verdict: H007 supported, committed at 0.80: no gene reaches a credible biallelic diagnosis only by rescuing a filtered call, and the BUB1B pair does not depend on any filter decision. H006 (retrospective) supported at 0.77: the panel's 20 filtered calls were correctly discarded, and the same conclusion holds at the coding-layer scale.
narrative.why: A variant caller's FILTER column is tuned for a genome-wide false-positive rate, not for one child's disease allele, so a true disease variant sitting in a hard-to-map region is exactly the kind of call it would suppress. Checking this against the already-annotated callset by SQL costs hours; ruling it out by re-calling from the raw sequencing reads costs a day. It has to be ruled out before the BUB1B pair can be trusted as complete, rather than one allele of a bigger picture the filters are hiding.

Seven of the eight keys are distinguishable by the returned numbers alone; the only pair the scorer cannot separate is {stop+unseen, missense+unseen}, which carried 0.17 of the prior mass. hypotheses.author: agharsallah
hypotheses.path: path 4 — the oracle as a measurement instrument
hypotheses.prediction: A submission whose rank-1 row holds exactly these two alleles returns full_match_rank = 1, rank_points = 100 and f_max = 1.0 from the challenge scorer.
hypotheses.reasoning: The oracle returned a full match at rank 1 for the pair row (submission 1, probe 1): the answer key is exactly the BUB1B stop_gained + missense pair. Confidence set by the reply, not the heuristic weighing; residual doubt is only the scorer's own correctness.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The scorer returns no full match for that row. A partial match (partial_match_rank = 1) would mean exactly one of the two alleles is causal and the other is not; no match at all would mean neither is.
hypotheses.statement: The causal compound-heterozygous pair is the BUB1B stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) together with the BUB1B missense allele absent from gnomAD, in trans.

hands_to.what: The confirmed pair is what Track 2 is allowed to argue from. Step 8's mechanism card was opened in parallel, but its verdicts waited for this reply, because a drug direction argued from an unconfirmed allele is a guess dressed as rigour. The reply also closes step 5 before it opens: no partner allele is missing, so there is nothing to recover from the reads.

inherits.what: The candidate pair itself comes from step 2's genome-wide coding scan, which left BUB1B as the only gene with two rare protein-altering alleles. Step 3 arrived at the same gene from the symptoms alone, without reading a variant, and step 4 showed nothing rare and protein-altering was hiding behind the quality filters. Step 1 supplies the thing that makes the upload legal at all: one spelling per variant, so an exact-match scorer can be trusted with the rows.

narrative.summary: The one step that could be wrong in public. Steps 2 to 4 had converged on a single BUB1B compound heterozygote, but converging is not confirming: every route read the same vendor callset, so four agreements could still be one mistake counted four times. This step spent the first of six irreversible oracle submissions on it — designed as a measurement rather than a guess, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a local replica of the scorer, and laid out so that seven of the eight possible replies would be told apart by the numbers that came back. The reply was a full match at rank 1: 100 rank points, F-max 1.000, threshold 0.9963.
narrative.verdict: H009 supported at confidence 1.00. The answer key is the BUB1B stop-gain plus missense pair, in trans, and phase is settled by the key itself rather than by reads — which is why step 5, the read-level recovery of a partner allele, never had to run. One of six submissions is spent; five remain, and they belong to iteration 2 and later.
narrative.why: The oracle is the only window onto the answer key, and it opens six times in total. A submission that cannot be decoded wastes one of those six: if two candidate pairs would produce the same rank_points and f_max, the reply says the answer was found but not which row found it. So the rows were chosen for distinguishability first and confidence second, and the whole design was written down before the upload — including what each possible reply would have meant. Matching is exact string equality on (chrom, pos, ref, alt), which is why step 1's normalization gates this step: a correct answer spelled differently scores zero.

steps.title: Knowledge and literature

entries.title: The Track 2 data layer: from the mechanism card to a first public-API snapshot

steps.goal: Which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism the confirmed alleles imply, and how strong is the evidence for each?

hypotheses.prediction: Public sources agree with the shape: ClinVar and the literature classify BUB1B MVA1 as autosomal recessive loss of function; every reported MVA1 genotype combines a null with a hypomorph or two hypomorphs; no BUB1B variant is annotated dominant or gain-of-function in ClinVar/OMIM; Reactome places BUB1B in the mitotic spindle checkpoint pathway.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any ClinVar or OMIM record of a dominant or gain-of-function BUB1B mechanism, functional evidence that kinase-domain missense alleles act as dominant negatives, or the oracle returning no match for the BUB1B pair (which would make the mechanism argument moot).
hypotheses.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

hypotheses.prediction: Open Targets knownDrugs for BUB1B, ChEMBL mechanisms for human BUB1B targets and DGIdb interactions for BUB1B return zero molecules with max_phase 4 (approved); approved molecules appear only for other targets in the expanded set (for example AURKB, KIF11, PLK1, TTK, HDAC1-3, HSP90AA1, MTOR, PRKAA1).
hypotheses.reasoning: First snapshot (078): three independent drug-target sources return no molecule for BUB1B at any phase; every approved drug in the table attaches to a pathway neighbour or a direction target. One measurement, three sources - the heuristic's 0.80 is a triage number, not a posterior. Re-weighed when the sources are refreshed or DrugBank becomes available.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any molecule with an approved status (ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label) whose recorded mechanism of action names BUB1B/BubR1 as the target.
hypotheses.statement: No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.

hands_to.what: Nothing further in iteration 1's own step map follows step 8. The confirmation it was waiting for did arrive: step 6 uploaded on 2026-09-09 and the oracle answered with a full match at rank 1 (entry 083), so the pair this card argues from is confirmed — the card's own files predate that reply by three days and still call the pair inferred. Per the strategy record the ranked candidate list and the final drug verdicts are produced once, after every Track 1 iteration has reported and its evidence is merged; that merge and the single Track 2 submission sit outside this iteration's step map, and iteration 2's step 7 is where the card was next revised.

inherits.what: the mechanism card is built from iteration 1's whole hypothesis record (H003–H009): the candidate gene and its two consequence classes from step 2, the phenotype corroboration from step 3, the ruling-out of a hidden filtered allele from step 4, the canonical variant spelling from step 1, and step 6's submission machinery that the ranking is waiting on before it can be argued.

narrative.summary: Wrote the Track 1 → Track 2 mechanism hand-off: BUB1B compound heterozygote (two different broken copies of the gene, one from each parent) — a stop-gained null allele plus a missense hypomorph (a partly working copy) — weakens the spindle assembly checkpoint (the mechanism that holds a dividing cell until every chromosome is attached), a loss of function with no gain-of-function component, and named four repurposing directions (reinforce the checkpoint, exploit aneuploidy stress, stabilise the hypomorph, prevent the child's tumour). Built a case-agnostic public-source data layer (`mva.drugs`) over Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed and openFDA; the first snapshot expanded 27 seed targets to 273 through 4 matched Reactome pathways and returned 3,766 drug-candidate rows (1,067 approved, 336 distinct approved drug names), 747 trials and 157 literature hits. Zero of those candidates target BUB1B/BubR1 directly at any clinical phase.
narrative.verdict: H011 supported, committed at 0.80: no market-approved drug acts directly on BUB1B/BubR1 across three independent sources; the 336 approved candidates all attach to pathway neighbours (TP53, MTOR, HSP90AA1, AURKB, CDK4/6, tubulin genes) or off-target directions. H010 stays proposed — only its pathway clause is tested (Reactome maps BUB1B to four checkpoint/kinetochore/mitotic pathways); its loss-of-function clause awaits ClinVar/OMIM and literature evidence.
narrative.why: Track 2 is a separately scored deliverable and the only part of this work that reaches the child directly — a repurposed drug is one already approved and available. A drug named without a cited mechanistic path from the confirmed allele to its target is worth nothing, so the mechanism card and a reproducible, provenance-tracked evidence layer had to exist before any candidate could be argued. Ranking and verdicts wait for step 6's oracle confirmation by design: arguing a drug direction from an unconfirmed allele is a guess dressed as rigour.
